G3-6 · Compatibility results: F2 on iOS 18.6, N3 on iOS 26.5

Needs your decision6 Nov · isolated test app, synthetic data, throwaway simulators (deleted) · G3-6 open

The same test app runs the approved ED-124 row natively: F2 styles on iOS 18.6, N3 Liquid Glass on iOS 26.5, Flutter content behind both. Every image is a genuine Simulator capture, labelled with its iOS version. Two test-app defects were fixed and re-run; one architecture limit (F1) needs your decision.

Findings Needs your decision

  • F1 · N3 Minimal capsule (architecture, iOS 26.5): the genuine tab bar caps a three-tab glass capsule at 274 pt (≈ 91 per tab) on a 402 pt phone; neither filling, item width nor a wider bar view changes it. Full (four tabs) fills 292 exactly. Options: (a) keep the 6 pt gap to the + and let the capsule start 39 from the left (recommended: keeps the approved + and bar relation); (b) centre it as now (30 left, 15 gap); (c) start at 21 with a 24 pt gap; (d) draw the Minimal bar in Flutter (not native, not recommended).
  • F2 · F2 Reduce Transparency (test app, fixed): the classic bar blur stays see-through; F2 must switch to a solid appearance itself. Rule added.
  • F3 · Day menu on other days (test app, fixed): a submenu header cannot be disabled; show Need more time as a disabled item when the day is not today.
  • F4 · Menu order: both menus use fixed element order so G2-9 and G2-8 read as approved when they open upward.
  • F5 · Accessibility listing on 26.5: each tab listed twice and no badge value; needs a VoiceOver check before implementation.
  • F6 · First launch on the 18.6 Simulator: Flutter took about 12 s to draw while shaders compiled (debug, Simulator). Environment, not architecture; check a release build on a device.
  • Still PENDING: iOS 16 and 17 (not tested; 18.6 does not verify them), every physical-device check, VoiceOver, Full Keyboard Access, Large Content Viewer, real-device performance.
